title: ci-slimmer-toolchain-prefetch-and-incremental-lint-adapter
author: Aisha Khan
description:
Motivation: Our presubmit pipelines have regressed in wall-clock time over the last six months due to an increasing number of heavy toolchain bootstrap steps and full-lint runs for large touches. This PR introduces two coordinated changes: (1) a minimal toolchain prefetch step that warms only requested tool caches based on changed files (language/tool affinity heuristics), and (2) an incremental lint adapter that runs full linters only when lint-affecting files are touched and otherwise runs a fast staged subset. Goals: reduce CI wall time for common small changes (target 30% median improvement on dev merges), reduce ephemeral runner bootstrap I/O, and make lint feedback faster for iterative development.

What this changes (high level):
- Introduce .github/actions/toolchain-prefetch action (scripts in .github/actions/toolchain-prefetch/*) which inspects the git diff, consults a lightweight language-to-tool manifest (ci/toolchain-map.yaml), and parallel-fetches only the images/artifacts required by affected modules.
- Add a small JSON artifact produced by the prefetch step (ci/toolchain-prefetch/metadata.json) to let downstream steps skip unneeded bootstraps.
- Replace monolithic lint job with lint:fast and lint:full. lint:fast executes staged linters (typos, import-order, small static checks) and uses a cache key tied to staged file list; lint:full is gated and only runs on pushes to main, release branches, or when lint:fast reports a potential gap.
- Update the composite test runner to accept the prefetch metadata and skip heavy toolchain init when possible.
- Docs: add ci/README-toolchain-prefetch.md with heuristics and guidance for adding new tool mappings.

Checklist:
- [x] Add toolchain-prefetch action with unit tests for diff-to-tool mapping.
- [x] Implement incremental lint adapter with fallback to full lint.
- [x] Wire prefetch metadata into build/test flow.
- [x] Add telemetry counters (ci/telemetry) for skipped bootstraps and lint fast-path hit-rate.
- [x] Run full test matrix in a nightly job to catch coverage gaps.

Testing and validation: The branch runs introduced an experimental presubmit lane (ci/presubmit/fast-path) for 48h on the main repo where ~65% of PRs used the fast-path and average presubmit time dropped from 14m -> 9m. Nightly full-matrix job ran unchanged; we added extra smoke runs for the adapter. We validated cache correctness with intentionally crafted diffs and confirmed the fast-lint produced identical results to full-lint on a randomized sample of 500 commits.

Rollout plan: staged rollout over two weeks. Feature flag in .github/workflows/presubmit.yaml to toggle fast-path. After 7 days monitor telemetry (fast-path hit-rate, CI wall-time distribution, flake count). On regression, toggle flag off and revert via hotfix branch.

Related: ENG-3821 (CI cost reduction), ENG-4022 (presubmit latency). Support ticket SUP-1142 requested faster iterations for SDK small changes.

Notes on safety: The lint adapter intentionally errs on the side of caution: when analysis is uncertain the workflow falls back to full-lint. Prefetch mapping is conservative and can be expanded by maintainers via ci/toolchain-map.yaml. There are added audit logs to trace why a given toolchain was or was not fetched.
commits: Introduce toolchain-prefetch composite action and unit tests
Wire prefetch metadata into presubmit composite-runner
Split lint job into lint:fast and lint:full and add adapter logic
Add ci/toolchain-map.yaml and README, telemetry counters
Fix: handle monorepo root-level changes -> always full-lint
Docs: add rollout and troubleshooting notes
review_comments: Evan Martinez (review): The mapping looks good but please add a fallback for ambiguous globs (e.g., '*' touches). Also add a short-circuit for changed files larger than 2000 LOC to force full-lint.
Aisha Khan (author): Added the short-circuit and tests; clarified ambiguous glob handling in README and added a linting opt-in annotation for exotic paths.

Gordon Lee (review): Can we ensure the prefetch step doesn't create noisy S3 requests? Suggest batching artifact HEAD checks and adding a 2s backoff. Also please add a 'prefetch.no-op' env var for local dev.
Aisha Khan (author): Implemented batching and backoff, and added the env var with docs. Pushed a follow-up commit that reduces S3 list calls in integration tests.
Lina Park (approval): Verified e2e in the experimental lane and smoke tests; approving pending telemetry thresholds in prod for 7d.
CI Bot: build/linux-unit-tests failed on commit 4 (flake). Reran and passed.
ci_history_notes: Note: one transient unit test flake in build/linux on first run; rerun fixed it. Nightly full-matrix telemetry added to catch regressions.
release_notes: Introduce toolchain prefetching to reduce presubmit bootstrap time and add an incremental lint adapter to speed up developer feedback loops. No user-facing API changes.
notes_for_rollback: Revert commit a3b9f7d7... or toggle presubmit fast-path flag in .github/workflows/presubmit.yaml. Telemetry and audit logs make it safe to verify before full revert.
high_risk_reasons: Low risk: changes are presubmit/build orchestration only. Potential risk: missing a lint check for edge cases; mitigated by conservative heuristics and nightly full runs.
